approved_text: Let S be the smallest set of integers containing 2 and 3 such that ab − 1 ∈ S whenever a and b are distinct elements of S. Does S have positive density?
draft: Let S be the smallest set of positive integers containing 2 and 3 such that whenever a and b are distinct elements of S, ab − 1 is also in S. Equivalently, S is the set of all integers that eventually appear when starting from 2, 3 and repeatedly appending a_i a_j − 1 (i ≠ j). Does S have positive density?
source_docstrings:
Let $a_1 = 2$ and $a_2 = 3$ and continue the sequence by appending to $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ all possible
values of $a_i a_j - 1$ with $i \neq j$.
Is it true that the set of integers which eventually appear has positive density?
